newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-DUTCH ABN TO BUY STAN FEDERAL FOR $1.9 BILLION.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-DUTCH ABN TO BUY STAN FEDERAL FOR $1.9 BILLION.

text.p: The Netherlands' leading bank ABN AMRO Holding NV said on Friday it agreed to pay a total $1.9 billion for Standard Federal Bancorporation Inc, the largest savings bank in the midwest United States.
The deal, under which ABN will offer $59 per share for all outstanding Standard Federal shares, is the Dutch bank's biggest acquisition to date.
ABN said it would issue $750 million in preference shares to help fund the acquisition.
"We intend to finance the transaction by means of an issue of $750 million preference shares in the United States through ABN AMRO North America Inc.," chairman Jan Kalff said in a statement.
"The remainder will be financed from ABN AMRO Holding NV's existing means."
Standard Federal, the fourth largest bank in the state of Michigan, employs some 4,000 staff and has 182 branches in Michigan, Ohio, Illinois and Indiana.
ABN AMRO said it had reached agreement with Standard Federal's board, but the deal still needed the approval of Standard Federal's shareholders and supervisory authorities.
The acquisition was expected to be finalised by mid-1997, ABN said, adding that the deal would contribute several tens of guilder cents to its earnings per share.
"On the basis of the expected 1997 profit of Standard Federal Bankcorp, the takeover will, once realised, contribute several tens of guilder cents to ABN AMRO's earnings per share," ABN AMRO said.
ABN AMRO said it would continue to comfortably meet the capital adequacy requirements of the Dutch central bank once the takeover had been consolidated.
ABN AMRO already has a United States banking arm, the LaSalle group, which has 130 branches in Illinois.
Standard Federal sells mainly savings products and home mortgages to its one million existing clients, ABN said.
At end-October, the U.S. bank had total assets of $15.5 billion and stockholder equity of around $900 million.
Standard Federal's banks will continue to operate under the Standard Federal name and ABN said there would be "significant cost savings" following the deal.
In Amsterdam, ABN AMRO shares gained 3.20 guilders ($1.89) each to to 108.50 guilders. ($ = 1.685 Dutch Guilders)
